title: Large coproducts descend from the derived category
statement: Let A be a locally w-small Grothendieck abelian category with a chosen w-Hom derived category. If D(A) has coproducts indexed by types in universe max(w,vA,vH), where vA is the Hom universe of A, then A has coproducts indexed at the same size. No preservation assertion for arbitrary derived coproducts is made.

source.place: Original proof step 1: agent-written derived-to-abelian coproduct transfer, extending Stacks Project Tag 0F5S

proof.text: For a family X_i form K, the coproduct of X_i[0] in D(A), and P=H^0(K). Applying H^0 to the injections gives the cofan X_i -> P. For each injective I, the degree-zero complex I[0] is K-injective, and exactness of Hom(-,I) identifies Hom_D(K,I[0]) with Hom_A(P,I). The derived coproduct property identifies this with product_i Hom_A(X_i,I), naturally in I.

For Y use an injective copresentation 0 -> Y -> I^0 -> I^1. The comparison Hom_A(P,-) -> product_i Hom_A(X_i,-) is natural and both sides are left exact. Its bijectivity on I^0 and I^1 implies bijectivity on their kernels, hence on Y. This is the coproduct universal property; the empty case gives a zero object.
